promptAsSent:
Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then stop. Do not write files, run commands or edit anything.

Attached reference images, in order:
Image 1: Geometry/layout authority: the edit target
Image 2: Family identity: finish and canopy design only; not layout
Image 3: Material/style only; not layout

Asset type: production-source master for a top-down game sprite: the chassis of the BULWARK, a heavy all-round anchor walking machine, in the old, low-tech Hegemony armour line, big brother of the Hound.

Image 1 is the exact silhouette and layout authority, a grey blockout: fill it in, never move, resize, widen or add to its shapes, and keep all empty canvas empty. From front to back: a small armoured head plate at the very front; the pilot canopy behind it; a broad, heavy, chamfered body box with wide shoulders; on each flank a darker rectangular shoulder pad, a flat riveted mounting plate with bolt points where a missile rack is bolted on later (nothing standing on it); a lighter flat deck down the spine with hatches; a wide engine block at the very rear with exhaust grilles. Thick glacis plates, heavy rivet rows, stowage boxes and grab handles. Symmetric about the vertical centre line.

Image 2 is family identity reference only, never layout: the accepted low-tech Hegemony HOUND, the light machine of the same line. Match it exactly in finish and parts: the same warm tan and khaki riveted plate with olive-green panels, the same rivet rows, weld seams, exposed pipe runs in the seams, worn bright edges and orange hazard panels on leading corners, and the SAME faceted pilot canopy: dark smoked grey-green glass panes, narrow at the front, split by thick riveted tan frame bars, in a hinged armour rim. Image 3 is material reference only: the Hegemony medium tank the line serves beside.

The lighter grey shape on the spine is the pilot canopy: draw it as that faceted framed canopy, filling the shape exactly. Old, low-tech, depot-built Hegemony military hardware: blunt, boxy, bolted and repairable, never sleek, smooth or high-tech.

Strict 90-degree zenith orthographic top-down view of the chassis top surfaces, the machine facing the TOP edge of the canvas. True transparent background, including all negative space; no ground, shadow slab, cast shadow, halo, glow, border, text, labels or logos. Draw only the chassis body: no weapons, missile racks, legs or feet, which are separate layers drawn later.

Avoid: sci-fi smooth plastic, glowing lights, bright blue or cyan, white paint, perspective, side view, isometric view, cropped edges, a second machine, text.
